Listen to this article Share Moshood Olanrewaju Bakare, the People’s Democratic Party (PDP), candidate for Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency in Kwara State, has pledged to strengthen partnerships with federal government agencies, Bank of Industry (BoI) and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN), to support local businesses if elected in the 2027 general elections. Advertisement Advertisement Bakare stated this on Thursday while presenting a speech titled, “Kwara at a Crossroads: The People, Our Challenges and the Path to a More Prosperous Future,” at the “News Keg”, a media interactive programme organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Kwara State council. The former member of the Kwara State House of Assembly, who chaired the House Committee on Public Accounts and later the Committee on Finance and Appropriation for two terms, said his legislative experience had prepared him for the responsibility of representing the constituency at the National Assembly. Read also: Court affirms Suswam as valid APC candidate for Benue North East senatorial election Outlining his economic development agenda, Bakare said he would pursue policies aimed at expanding employment opportunities, promoting entrepreneurship and improving access to development finance for youths and small business owners. He also promised to canvass improved agricultural inputs, modern farming equipment, processing facilities, storage systems and better market access for farmers across the constituency. Advertisement The PDP candidate mentioned eight pillars of his proposed legislative agenda as Security and Community Protection; Health for All; Education and Human Capital Development; Youth Empowerment and Employment; Agriculture and Rural Development; MSME and Industrial Development; Infrastructure and Accountability; and Accessible Representation. He said the constituency’s economic potential required targeted interventions, particularly in agriculture, commerce and traditional industries. Advertisement Read also: Senate seeks prosecution of candidates whose supporters engage in political violence “Offa’s leather industry, Ifelodun’s agricultural potential and Oyun’s commercial and agricultural opportunities must receive deliberate attention. I will pursue partnerships with relevant federal agencies, the Bank of Industry and SMEDAN to support local businesses, improve access to financing and stimulate economic activities,” he said. Advertisement Advertisement Speaking on his legislative experience, Bakare highlighted his involvement in the financial restructuring of Kwara State during the Eighth Assembly, particularly the establishment of the Kwara State Internal Revenue Service (KW-IRS). He said that the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR) stood at between N500 million and N600 million monthly at the time, necessitating reforms to strengthen revenue collection, improve accountability and reduce dependence on borrowing. According to him, the establishment of KW-IRS was part of efforts to build a more efficient revenue administration system and enhance the state’s financial capacity. He maintained that sustainable development could only be achieved through sound policies, effective institutions and responsible management of public resources. Read also: 60 days to election: Only 3 of 18 presidential candidates publish 2027 manifestos Bakare stressed that his ambition was not merely to occupy a seat in the House of Representatives but to ensure that the position translated into tangible benefits for the people. “As I seek the mandate to represent Ifelodun, Offa and Oyun in the House of Representatives, I am presenting myself not only as someone with legislative experience and administrative exposure, but also as one committed to building a constituency where people are heard, their needs are addressed and their future is protected. “My ambition is not simply to occupy a seat in the National Assembly. It is to make that seat count for every constituent,” he said.
